sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: one-way versus two-way street sides, placard versus occupant, hill checklist order, parallel parking wheel turns and exit habits
Confusable pairs among the parking rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Street side depends on the street type: a one-way street normally allows parking on either side, while a two-way street forbids parking on the left side. [A01]
Why it matters: group street sides; confusable one-way versus two-way; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Showing a disability placard or plates is not enough by itself; the reserved space also needs a person with a physical disability riding in the car or being dropped off or picked up. [A01]
Why it matters: group disability parking; confusable placard versus occupant; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A02
Two separate offenses apply around reserved spaces: parking in the access aisle, and using another person's placard or plates when that person is not being carried. [A02]
Why it matters: group disability parking; confusable aisle versus placard misuse; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
Leaving the transmission in gear applies to a manual car, while an automatic is left in park, and in both cases the parking brake is set. [A01]
Why it matters: group securing the vehicle; confusable manual versus automatic; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
In parallel parking the wheel turns run sharp right, then sharp left, then sharp right again as you pull toward the curb. [A02]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; confusable order of wheel turns; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
The hill checklist on this page uses the words emergency or parking brake for the same brake that must be set on any parked vehicle. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; glossary parking brake.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A01
The reason for turning the wheels toward the roadside on a hill is so the car rolls away from traffic if it starts to move. [A01]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable with the hill graphic on the next page.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A01
Opening a door on the street side is allowed only after you check traffic first, since getting out on the curb side is preferred. [A01]
Why it matters: group exiting; confusable driver side versus passenger side; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A02
Parking on hills ends with the same security habit as any other stop: take the key out of the ignition, lock up, and keep the keys with you. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; continuation of securing the vehicle.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A02
During parallel parking the final position is the center of the space, not pressed against the car ahead or behind. [A02]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A01
Colored curb markings can signal a parking limit even where no sign is posted, and a curb painted yellow means no parking there. [A01]
Why it matters: group no-parking zones; confusable sign versus curb paint; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]
